preamble: Rhotacization of the palatalized (slender) nasal [nʲ] to a palatalized rhotic [ɾʲ] in initial clusters is a regular Goidelic development. In Connacht and Ulster Irish, a coronal nasal after a non-sibilant consonant (c, g, m, t) became a rhotic, while Munster Irish keeps the nasal; Scottish Gaelic shares the change (Old Irish gním > gnìomh /ɡ̥ɾʲĩə̃v/, cnes > cneas /kʰɾʲẽs̪/). Because Goidelic keeps a broad/slender contrast, slender nʲ gives slender ɾʲ, as in gníomh 'deed' and cneasta 'decent'. The broad counterpart (cnoc [kɾˠʊk] 'hill', mná [mˠɾˠaː] 'women') is the same rule. The Goidelic outcome is a tap or approximant [ɾʲ] rather than a trill.

examples.from: Old Irish gním; Munster gníomh /ɟnʲiːvˠ/ 'action, deed'
examples.note: Slender nʲ after g becomes slender ɾʲ, with nasality left on the following vowel in Ulster.

examples.note: When t-prothesis puts a stop before slender n, the nasal is realized as ɾʲ (Donegal, Mayo and Connemara).
